subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: Should Gateway/Codex keep immediate `chat.send` `started` semantics for Codex native-thread sessions, or must it preflight/rotate/fail visibly before ACK when native thread liveness is uncertain?
rationale: The source shows the public ACK happens before durable user-turn/dispatch proof, while Codex native thread repair crosses provider-runtime ownership and can change user-visible RPC semantics.

options.title: Pre-ACK Liveness Guard
options.body: Before returning `started`, rotate an unsafe oversized binding when possible and otherwise fail visibly if no runnable Codex native thread can be established.

options.title: ACK Then Async Failure
options.body: Preserve immediate ACK but add a durable failure event, health/audit signal, and UI-visible error if dispatch or Codex `turn/start` does not begin promptly.

options.title: Prove Existing Mitigations
options.body: Keep current semantics only if a live or fixture replay of the reported persisted state proves the merged rotation and compaction fixes now cover it.

recommendation.title: Pre-ACK Liveness Guard
recommendation.body: Before returning `started`, rotate an unsafe oversized binding when possible and otherwise fail visibly if no runnable Codex native thread can be established.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current merged native-thread overflow rotation path that would likely be extended or constrained by the chosen contract.
